text:
K'Andre Miller is a Stanley Cup winner now, and on a Carolina team that owns the puck, he is mostly along for a very good ride. Carolina takes about 62% of the shot attempts and expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, and he plays 22 minutes a night. His top skating speed is in the 99th percentile of NHL players.

The point total is quiet: one goal and eight points in 23 games, with one goal on 35 shots. That shooting rate (2.9%) is well below what we'd expect from him, so a couple more goals should come. Four assists in his last ten, including two in the Global Series in Finland, are why fantasy waiver columns from Yahoo Sports and others started listing him this week.

Keep it in proportion, though. Evolving-Hockey noted that his teammates last season ranked in the 97th percentile by their impact, which flatters raw on-ice numbers, and had him worth 0.8 wins, mostly from even-strength defense. Our range sees about 34 points by season's end: a useful top-four defenseman on a team that makes everyone look good.
